newsitem.title: FRANCE: East Timorese to leave French embassy for Portugal.
newsitem.headline: East Timorese to leave French embassy for Portugal.

text.p: Four East Timorese men broke into the French embassy in Jakarta on Tuesday to seek political asylum will be allowed to leave for Portugal, the French Foreign Ministry said.
"The four Timorese should leave for Portugal today or tomorrow," ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux told reporters.

Since September 1995, 96 young East Timorese who have broken into foreign embassies in Jakarta have been given asylum in Portugal, the former colonial power in the enclave invaded by Indonesia in December 1975.

The four scaled the three-metre (nine-foot) high spiked iron fence surrounding the French embassy compound in central Jakarta, unfurling a banner while shouting "Viva East Timor" and other pro-independence slogans.
East Timorese sources identified the men as Ru Ximenes, 26, Akilis Siqueira, 21, Bonifacio Cardoso Diaz, 18, and Siquito Valenti, all from Los Palos on the eastern tip of the territory.
Two of the four said they were high school students while the other two said they were students at the University of East Timor in Dili.

The break-in came before talks between the seven-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the European Union (EU) in Singapore next week where East Timor has been raised a possible sticking point.
The United Nations does not recognise Indonesia's 1976 annexation of East Timor and regards Portugal as the administering power in the territory.
